solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 7's 'pots and pans'?

parts.note: the percussion section of an orchestra is nicknamed the kitchen, so a percussionist's pots and pans are the gear of that section, as well as real cooking pots

explanation.surface: A drummer's battered kit is jokingly called his pots and pans.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 refers to 7-down, PERCUSSIONIST. Orchestral players call the percussion section 'the kitchen', so the clue's quoted pots and pans are both cookware and that section's instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots and pans are the classic examples of cooking utensils, the household items this word covers.

clue.text: River of stars?

definitions.meaning: a great river of Pakistan flowing to the Arabian Sea
a faint southern constellation, the Indian, is a group of stars with this Latin name

explanation.surface: A poetic phrase for the Milky Way, a river made of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to the Asian river and to a southern constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: 'Schon Rosmarin' — oddly right for such a craft

indicators.note: oddly here means taking every other letter of the quoted title, skipping the odd-numbered ones

explanation.surface: Schön Rosmarin, a Kreisler violin piece, is claimed as fitting music for some vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps the alternate letters of the title read as one run (the 2nd, 4th, 6th...), giving CORSAI; R for right completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate ship of the Barbary coast, so it is a kind of sailing vessel.

clue.text: Kind of dashes round outskirts of Bristol to win badge

indicators.note: round means the two dash letters sit either side of the next piece

parts.note: an em dash is the long dash in printing, and two of them, plural dashes, give EM twice

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of Bristol are taken

explanation.surface: Racing around the edge of Bristol in order to earn a badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of dashes' is em dashes: two EMs, placed 'round' BL, the outer letters of Bristol.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a symbolic device or badge worn or displayed to show identity or allegiance.

clue.text: Royalty in knots?

definitions.meaning: the British royal family has used this house name since 1917
a Windsor is a wide, symmetrical way of tying a necktie, so ties done that way are such knots

explanation.surface: Royals all tied up in knots, perhaps over a family crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal house took the name of its castle, and the broad tie knot was named after a duke of that house.

clue.text: Sally's inscription on bone leads to thoughtful examination

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; a sally is a witty retort

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the inscription on a gravestone
OS is Latin for bone, a common crossword abbreviation

indicators.note: leads are the front letters, so the first letters of thoughtful and examination are taken

explanation.surface: Someone called Sally's carving on bone prompts a careful study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' is not a girl but a witty comeback; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty remark, and a sharp retort in reply is exactly that.

clue.text: I sus inspector out — he's a big hitter!

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order, a rearrangement of the fodder before it

explanation.surface: Someone says they have rumbled the inspector, who is a forceful man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sus out' looks like the phrasal verb meaning to figure out, but 'out' is the anagram signal on I SUS INSPECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer or timpanist spends his performance striking instruments, so he hits things for a living.

clue.text: 7's implement getting group of scientists in muddle

indicators.note: in means the scientists' letters go inside the muddle

parts.note: a tangle is a muddle or confused mess
RI is the Royal Institution, a London body of scientists

explanation.surface: A drummer's tool causes confusion among a team of researchers.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is 7-down, PERCUSSIONIST. RI, the Royal Institution, is a British scientific society.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a steel percussion instrument struck with a beater, one of the orchestral percussionist's kit.

clue.text: Stuffed again with queer-looking strudel — hope sappers are on top of it!

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of means this piece sits above the rest

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the army corps whose soldiers are called sappers

indicators.note: queer-looking means odd in appearance, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd-shaped strudel is refilled, with army engineers hoped to be in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are the soldiers of the Royal Engineers, RE; 'queer-looking' is the anagram signal, and 'are on top of it' places RE above the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture is padded with stuffing, so re-covering and refilling a chair is stuffing it once more.

clue.text: 25 characters from Daniel Deronda

indicators.note: characters are letters, and these are taken from inside the novel's title

explanation.surface: Twenty-five characters drawn from George Eliot's novel Daniel Deronda.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to 25-down, meaning a senior person. 'characters' looks like people in the novel but means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An older person or senior is someone's senior in age, which this word expresses.

clue.text: General finds equal among British — near Darjeeling mostly?

indicators.note: among means the equal phrase sits between the other letters
mostly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Darjeeling is a fine Indian tea
on a par means equal or level

explanation.surface: A general finds his match among the British near the tea gardens of Darjeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' takes TEA (Darjeeling) to TE; ON A PAR goes 'among' B and TE. 'near' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was the most famous French general, known by his surname.

clue.text: Trawl round America for 7's implement

indicators.note: round means the trawling phrase goes around the next letter

parts.note: to trawl for fish is to cast nets

explanation.surface: Fishing all around America in search of a drummer's tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is 7-down, PERCUSSIONIST.
explanation.definitionFit: These clicking shells of wood, held in the hand, are a percussion instrument played in Spanish dance music.

clue.text: Floated quietly in flood

parts.note: to have swum is close to having floated in water
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone drifted silently on floodwater.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to drench or inundate with water, as a flood does.

clue.text: Bribe criminal bounders to leave Delaware

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Delaware

explanation.surface: Corrupt cads are paid off to get out of Delaware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes DE from BOUNDERS; 'criminal' rearranges what remains, BOUNRS.
explanation.definitionFit: To suborn is to induce someone, often by paying them, to commit a crime such as perjury.

clue.text: 7's implement's in fish barrel

definitions.note: the final 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: the bass is a sea fish
a drum is a barrel-shaped container, as for oil

explanation.surface: A drummer's instrument has ended up inside a barrel of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is 7-down, PERCUSSIONIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The large low-pitched drum of an orchestra or band is a mainstay of the percussionist's kit.

clue.text: Figure (on the 24?) which doesn't strike a chord at once

definitions.text: Figure (on the 24?) which doesn't strike a chord at once

parts.words: Figure (on the 24?) which doesn't strike a chord at once
parts.note: a musical figure in which the notes of a chord are played one after another rather than together, here on 24, a xylophone

explanation.surface: A shape on the xylophone that fails to ring an immediate bell with listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't strike a chord' sounds like 'isn't familiar', but literally means the chord's notes are not struck together. 24 is 24-across, XYLOPHONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken chord, its notes sounded in succession, is a standard musical figure or pattern.

clue.text: Plant's unexpected gain, stocking smoked fish with hint of incense

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: stocking means holding within, so the fish and incense letters go inside
unexpected suggests the letters fall in a surprising order

parts.note: lox is smoked salmon

indicators.note: a hint is a small trace, so only the first letter of incense is used

explanation.surface: A surprising windfall: a stock of smoked fish with a whiff of incense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' arranges the four letters as GNIA, and 'stocking' puts the fish and the I between its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tropical South American plant, grown indoors for its velvety bell-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Loads of Latins dancing, large and small

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Plenty of Latin Americans dancing, both big and little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loads' looks like a noun meaning lots but is the verb, as when loading software.
explanation.definitionFit: To load a program onto a computer is to set it up there, the same as putting it in place.

clue.text: Reduce rating on area of high pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
a ridge is a long area of high atmospheric pressure on a weather map

explanation.surface: Lower one's assessment when a high-pressure zone arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like an assessment but is a sailor, AB.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book is to shorten or cut it down while keeping its sense.

clue.text: Drugs stashed in footwear?

definitions.meaning: stimulants such as amphetamines are slang called this
the top parts of shoes, above the soles, are called this

explanation.surface: Narcotics hidden inside a pair of shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimulant pills pick a user up, hence the slang, while a shoe's top section is its upper part.

clue.text: Conveyed — like haggis or gas?

definitions.meaning: carried or transmitted, as along a channel
the haggis is brought in to a Burns Night supper behind a bagpiper, while gas is supplied by pipe

explanation.surface: Something carried in, the way a haggis or a gas supply arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: At a Burns Night supper, the Scottish celebration of the poet Burns, the haggis is ceremonially led in by a bagpiper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carried in through a pipe, or led in by a piper, has been brought in.

clue.text: Privy Councillor's first to waste time

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to lose time is to waste it

explanation.surface: A member of the Privy Council is the first to fritter away time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privy Councillor' reads as one title, but 'Privy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Privy and this word both mean private or secret, and both can also name a small toilet.

clue.text: Rock bottom, Adrian! Head off and work!

indicators.note: to work something is to manipulate it, so the letters are reshaped
the head of a name is its opening letter, and off says that letter is removed before the rest is reworked

explanation.surface: A boss tells Adrian he has hit rock bottom and to stop daydreaming and work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' removes the first letter of the name; 'work' then rearranges the remaining five, DRIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything, like the point directly below an observer, is its absolute low.

clue.text: Cross yard to cut and polish 7's implement

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross
to lop is to cut off
to hone is to sharpen or refine

explanation.surface: An instruction to cross the yard, trim and shine a drummer's instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is 7-down, PERCUSSIONIST.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument of tuned wooden bars struck with mallets belongs to the percussion section.

clue.text: Senior serviceman stripped

indicators.note: stripped means the outer layer is removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a soldier is a serviceman in the army

explanation.surface: An older soldier has been stripped, perhaps of rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' suggests demotion, but it removes the outer letters of SOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old person, a senior citizen, is informally called this.

clue.text: Early intelligence has numbers admitting: 'Almost ruined'

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the shortened word goes inside

parts.note: musical numbers are songs

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: undid means ruined, as in 'that undid him'

explanation.surface: Preliminary information includes figures that confess something was nearly wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' looks like figures but means songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundings are preliminary enquiries made to test opinion before acting, so they give early information.

clue.text: Steer clear of this type of truck

definitions.meaning: An American make of trucks and vans

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid a particular kind of lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to evade, and the US brand founded by the Dodge brothers builds trucks.

clue.text: Authorised carer making notes, maybe

definitions.note: banknotes are an example, so the definition is plural in sense while the answer is a mass noun

parts.note: legal means authorised by law
a tender is one who tends or looks after

explanation.surface: A licensed care worker takes notes on a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests jottings, but means banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are currency that must by law be accepted in payment of debts, an instance of official money.
